title: analytics: a dashboard global filter whose field shares a dataset dimension's name is lowered to that dimension — the spec says it resolves against the dataset object
body:
Filing class: ① product defect (spec ↔ runtime contradiction) — reach: a dashboard's global filter, measured once on `@objectstack/*` 18.1.0 by the objectstack-ai/hotclm #109 dev (PR objectstack-ai/hotclm#128 Acceptance notes). **Reader:** objectstack triage.

## Symptom
`GlobalFilterSchema.field` is documented to resolve against the dataset's **object**, not its dimensions (#16256, closed; #16268 made the docs example stop sharing a name for the same reason). At runtime the opposite happens when the names collide.

hotclm's `contract_metrics` dataset (object `clm_contract`) had a dimension `{ name: 'department', field: 'department.name' }`, and the legal workbench a global filter `{ field: 'department', type: 'lookup', optionsFrom: sys_business_unit }`. Picking a department sent `runtimeFilter { department: <unit id> }`, which `@objectstack/service-analytics` 18.1.0 `executeSelection` lowered to `WHERE department.name = <unit id>` — every widget read 0. A filter key that is not a dimension name (`our_entity`) compiles to the raw column, as documented.

## Expected
A global filter's `field` resolves against the dataset object's field, as the spec says, whatever the dataset's dimensions are named; or, if dimension-first is intended, the spec text and `dashboard-filter-field-unknown` say so and the build flags the collision.

The app renamed its dimension (`department_name`, like its `contract_type_name`), so nothing is blocked; this card is for the next author who meets it silently.

## Dedupe
MCP `search_issues` on this repo: `dashboard global filter runtimeFilter resolves through dataset dimension name instead of object field lookup id` → 7 hits: #16256 and #16268 (closed — the documented rule this contradicts), #14275, #7804, #3365, #5144, #20644 (closed, different). None reports the runtime half.

---
_Filed by the `repo:hotclm` PM seat from a dev report._
